Attaching the first-pass artifacts: monthly-kpi-dashboard-2029-04.pdf (slice) and latency-trace-spotcheck.png (sample). Summary below.

Quick findings (first pass):
- Model routing: 92% of requests still on the low-latency variant, but a small cohort (~8%) has shifted to a higher-cost/higher-latency variant over last 9 days. That cohort aligns to queries with long context lengths.
- Cache misses: KV cache miss rate increased from 4.1% to 9.8% on the highest-volume prefix set (likely due to a prompt template change at the customer).
- Infra: no clear host-level OOMs or instance reboots in the window; slight increase in GPU scheduling delay during peak (median queue add time +18ms).

Hypotheses prioritized: 1) prompt/template change causing more long-context work -> routing into larger model variant, 2) prefix cache churn from new prompt variants, 3) demand burst edges causing small queueing.

Immediate mitigations we've tested in staging:
- Short-term: pin high-volume routes to the low-latency variant for the next 48h (config flag), and increase KV cache TTL for the affected prefix set to reduce cache churn.
- Medium: suggest a canary rollback of the prompt change on NorthStar side if pinning is not viable.

Action items (owners):
- Jonas: finalize the dashboard PDF and add a one-slide root-cause for QBR (due 9 May).
- Karthik: verify the cache TTL change and report expected delta on token-costs.
- Irene: stand by for a Friday 30-min bridge; prepare sample traces and span-level timings.

Atts: monthly-kpi-dashboard-2029-04.pdf (PDF, 210KB), latency-trace-spotcheck.png (PNG, 560KB)
